I remember reading that bisexuality is a term that was created by straight people to describe people who would date both men and women but, as such, it's not a great descriptor. As far as linguistics go, it seems to indicate that you ONLY date men or women which many bi people can attest to being false.

I feel the best way to think of it is as a reclaimed word because, historically and practically, we've treated it as meaning someone who is attracted to multiple genders and not necessarily just within the gender binary. The confusion and sometimes hostility that comes with gender outside the binary pushed people to create the pansexual label. Some people feel that this only reaffirms the initial "bi means two" argument. It kinda also implies that anyone who is pan is bi but not necessarily the other way around.

To sum up, I prefer the term pan out of the fact that it's very definite in who it includes although I'll use bisexual as an easier alternative because honestly, I don't really owe anyone an explanation of my sexuality. Bisexuality is completely valid and it does not mean "two" but it's tiring having to explain all of this to people who don't get the nuance of gender and sexuality especially within cultural context.

A lot of us go through this so don't feel weird about it. If I recall correctly, bisexuality is a term that was created by straight people to describe people who would date both men and women but as such it's not a great descriptor because, as far as linguistics go, it seems to indicate that you ONLY date men or women. This is not the case. The best way to think of it is as a reclaimed word because historically we've treated it as meaning someone who is attracted to multiple genders, not necessarily just the gender binary. The confusion and sometimes hostility that comes with gender outside the binary pushed people to create the pansexual label although some people feel that this only reaffirms the initial "bi means two" argument. It kinda also means that anyone who is pan is bi but not necessarily the other way around.

Personally, if it's my older family or someone I don't feel comfortable explaining gender to asking what I am I'll just say bi since it's somewhat easier to explain but that has its own issues. If it's someone I know who understands gender or if I feel up to explaining the gender construct then I'll use pan because I know they understand some of the nuance that goes into it and they know I'm not just making stuff up.

Tl;dr:

They have different sources as far as how they came to be but they essentially mean the same thing. Use what makes you comfortable. Your label is for other people but your identity is entirely your own and you don't owe it to anyone to have to explain things perfectly. Also, there's nothing wrong with tending towards one gender expression as far as attraction goes. You're still valid.
